summary: Built AccessDeniedPage as a standalone routed screen (src/pages/AccessDeniedPage.jsx, route /access-denied) matching the repo's established dark-theme chrome: breadcrumb header, centered alert card with red warning icon, the exact copy 'You do not have permission to view this page.', and a 'Back to Dashboard' link to '/'. It also auto-redirects to '/' after 3s so direct-link access per UC10-AF-002/UC11-AF-001/UC11-BR-012 never leaves the denial screen rendered indefinitely. No network calls are made by this page itself (it renders no Tracker/Settings data by design). Lint, full test suite (111 tests incl. 3 new ones) and production build all pass; verified visually via Playwright screenshot against a running dev server.

pr.title: feat(ui-gen): AccessDeniedPage for Tracker and Settings/Admin direct-link blocking
pr.body: Implements AccessDeniedPage (UC10-AF-002, UC11-AF-001, UC11-BR-012): a standalone full-screen page shown when a user without a permitted role hits a direct link to the Tracker or Settings/Admin screens. Shows the exact required message, renders none of the blocked screen's content, offers a manual link back to the Dashboard, and auto-redirects after a short delay. Routed at /access-denied in App.jsx. No other module's files were touched.

blockers: None of the six TARGET DESIGN images (IMG-1..IMG-6) actually depict an access-denied state: IMG-1 shows the populated Tracker screen and IMG-2..IMG-6 show the populated Settings/Admin screens and their dialogs (Add User, Add Approval Matrix Rule) — content that belongs to the lifecycle-uc10-uc11 Tracker/Settings pages, not to this task's AccessDeniedPage. Since no screenshot shows the actual denial screen to reproduce pixel-for-pixel, I built AccessDeniedPage using this repo's already-established visual language for permission-denied states (see src/features/contract-repository/components/AccessDeniedView.jsx and the inline access-denied block in src/pages/EsignatureSettingsPage.jsx): dark background, breadcrumb header, centered card with a red warning icon, and an emerald primary CTA — plus the exact copy and redirect behavior the acceptance criteria specify.

The Tracker and Settings/Admin pages themselves (TrackerPage, SettingsAdminPage) are not yet built in this repo (no /tracker or /settings-admin routes exist), so this task could not wire a real route guard that renders AccessDeniedPage when an unauthorized role requests those paths — that wiring is out of this task's scope ('AccessDeniedPage' only) and belongs with whichever task builds TrackerPage/SettingsAdminPage. AccessDeniedPage was registered at its own route, '/access-denied', so it is reachable and testable now; the guard's navigate(..., { state: { accessDeniedMessage } }) call should target this route once those pages exist.

Inferred field: AccessDeniedPage reads an optional `location.state.accessDeniedMessage` string (falling back to the default 'You do not have permission to view this page.') so a future Tracker/Settings guard can pass a role-specific message, matching the existing NewContractAccessGuard pattern in src/features/contracts/components/NewContractAccessGuard.jsx. This field is not declared in any DTO in context.json — it is local router state, not an API contract, inferred from the design pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase.

This task calls no API endpoints (AccessDeniedPage renders only static content on blocked access, per the acceptance criteria that no Tracker/Settings data of any kind reach the user), so the GET endpoints listed in the task's 'API endpoints you must call' section (tracker/ownership, cycle-time, bottleneck, turnaround, settings/users) were not wired into this component — wiring them here would contradict the acceptance criteria that none of that data is ever exposed to a blocked user.
